_comment: Symbols that are registered in ported.json AND whose original machine code must survive,
renamed, so the C++ can call it. tools/asm.py renames the PROC instead of padding it out.
This is the OpenGL activation's fallback mechanism. A function needs a -gl branch, which
means it must be registered, which normally pads the original away and forces the else arm
to be a hand transcription. For gfxBitmap::Load that would mean porting four pixel-format
converters and a lock/convert/unlock loop before anything is drawn at all.
Calling the original instead is both cheaper and stricter. agigl/glswitch.h requires that
with -gl absent the process does EXACTLY what it does today; running the 1999 machine code
is the only way to guarantee that rather than hope a transcription is faithful.
The value is the alias stem. tools/asm.py prefixes it with _arts_orig_ to form the MASM
label, which is the decorated form of the cdecl extern "C" name the C++ declares - so
gfxBitmap_Load here is _arts_orig_gfxBitmap_Load in the assembly and
arts_orig_gfxBitmap_Load in C++. gfx/origfallback.h holds those declarations.
Anything listed here is a function whose C++ is NOT yet a full reimplementation. Removing
an entry is the last step of porting one properly, and the entry should go the moment the
else arm becomes a real transcription.
